definition: Frenetic means fast-moving and energetic in a wild, scattered, barely controlled way.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word frenetic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know frenetic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: By its final hour the toy drive turned frenetic — volunteers sprinting between bins, tape guns firing, and a foreman calling out numbers no one had time to write down.
Hectic is milder than frenetic — a packed, demanding stretch that still more or less follows its schedule, before the wildness sets in.
Frantic goes further than frenetic: fear or desperation takes the wheel, and the wild motion becomes a scramble to escape disaster.

Frenzied means whipped into uncontrolled excitement — the crowd, the mob, the feeding sharks. Frenetic is its everyday workplace cousin: the same wildness of motion, but usually still aimed at getting something done. A frenetic kitchen is out of breath, not out of its mind.

Breakneck is about one thing only: dangerous speed. A breakneck descent can be perfectly controlled the whole way down. Frenetic adds disorder to the speed — motion scattering in every direction as the plan loses its grip.

and is over by 5:15, and nothing in between happens slowly.

To a first-time visitor the half hour looks frenetic past saving: buyers wading between crates, auctioneers running three sales at once, ice carts cutting through the aisles, numbers shouted over other numbers.
Every lot sold gets a price, every price gets a buyer's mark, and no crate is lifted twice.
'Fast is fine,' the auction master says, tapping the board.
'Lost is not.' By breakfast the dock is hosed clean, the ledgers agree, and the wildest half hour on the coast has once again added up.
